newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain, UAE to boost labour and social cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain, UAE to boost labour and social cooperation.

text.p: Bahrain's Labour and Social Affairs Minister Abdel-Nabi al-Shula will visit the United Arab Emirates later this month for talks to boost labour and social affairs cooperation.
A labour ministry statement said Shula, leading a high-level delegation, would fly to the UAE capital Abu Dhabi on February 22. He will also visit Dubai.

"We hope that during our meetings with the representatives of the private sector in the UAE, a formula for more effective utilisation of human resources in both states can be developed," Shula said in the statement.

"The private sector in the UAE, with its dynamic and future-oriented outlook, can be an active partner in our efforts to provide training facilities and programmes of internationally accepted standards to GCC nationals," he added.
The UAE and Bahrain are members of the GCC, a political and economic alliance which also groups Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait.
Bahrain has embarked on an ambitious training programme to find more jobs for Bahrainis to combat rising unemployment which has helped fuel anti-government unrest over the last two years.

Other GCC states have also begun a drive to find jobs for their citizens and reduce their reliance on expatriates. A Gulf official said in December foreign workers accounted for more than 80 percent, and in some cases 90 percent, of labourers in some GCC industries.
